- A key declared in `config.yaml` is file-owned. The UI, `POST /config/update`, and `POST /config/field/update` return 400 naming the key, the section, any ignored DB value, and the resolution.
- A key the file does not declare becomes DB-owned once `store_model_in_db` is on; the UI writes it to `LiteLLM_Config`.
- Re-sending the value the file already holds is accepted, because nothing changes.
- `model_list` is not merged: a UI-added model is an extra deployment in `LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable`, load-balanced alongside a same-named YAML entry.

The refusal body is explicit, so a UI error is diagnosable:

```json
{"detail": {"error": "general_settings key 'store_model_in_db' is set in the config file and cannot be changed here.",
  "keys": ["store_model_in_db"], "section": "general_settings", "stored_database_values_ignored": [],
  "resolution": "edit /app/config.yaml to change it, or remove it from the file to let the database own it"}}
```

Before v1.103.0 precedence was reversed — the database deep-merged over YAML — so on older versions edit the UI value, not the file.

Two details for anyone automating the same writes: `/config/update` is documented as "For Admin UI - allows admin to update config via UI" and rejects every role except `proxy_admin` with `403 Only proxy admins can update config` (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:21154-21175`). `/config/field/update` returns the same 400 when no database is connected, before it validates the field name (`:21457`).

## 5. Browser versus API

The browser session is a UI convenience, not a second authorization model: after login the UI calls the ordinary management endpoints with its session credential and the proxy applies the same role checks used for curl (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:21154-21175`). Anything the UI cannot change because of file ownership also cannot be changed by API — that is the point of the 400 above.

- Configuration that must survive a rebuild and be reviewed in Git: `config.yaml`.
- Entities that change at runtime per customer or app — keys, teams, users, MCP servers, DB models: UI/API into Postgres.
- Never both for the same key.

`POST /login` is the hidden form handler (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:20106`).

| Path | Credential | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Environment | `UI_USERNAME` (default `admin`), `UI_PASSWORD`; master key accepted as password when `UI_PASSWORD` is unset (`litellm/proxy/auth/login_utils.py:149-160`) | Anyone logging in this way is a proxy admin |
| Database user | password set via `Internal Users` or `POST /user/new` | role comes from the DB |
| SSO | `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GENERIC_CLIENT_ID` | `[Enterprise]` — without a license startup fails with "You must be a LiteLLM Enterprise user to use SSO" (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/ui_sso.py:5168-5172`); free up to 5 users (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/enterprise.md`) |

# 12 — Management API

Scope: the HTTP surface that creates keys, teams, users, models, and settings on a running gateway. `[OSS]` except organization routes and SCIM, which need `LITELLM_LICENSE`. These are FastAPI routes on the same app as inference (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:23211-23250`): one base URL, one auth header.

## 1. Shape and authentication

Management paths are unprefixed (`/key/generate`, `/team/new`); inference keeps `/v1/...` on separate routers. Every management route declares `dependencies=[Depends(user_api_key_auth)]` (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py:2438-2441`); authorization is a role check inside the handler, not a scope system.

- **Master key** (`Authorization: Bearer sk-...`): the proxy admin credential (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/deploy.md`), resolving to an admin identity without a Virtual Key model allowlist (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/master_key_rotations.md`).
- **Virtual keys**: act only on routes their role and object permissions allow; `/key/generate` accepts non-admin callers only for their own `user_id` (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py:2462-2470`).
- **Admin-only handlers** answer `403 Admin-only endpoint. Not allowed to access this.` (`litellm/types/proxy/common_proxy_errors.py:11`); `/config/update` has its own string, `403 Only proxy admins can update config` (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:21154-21175`).

Mutations are audited via the `litellm-changed-by` header (`:2448-2451`). No route takes an idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout mints a second key (`:2438-2453`).

| Teams | `POST /team/new`, `/team/update`, `/team/delete`; `GET /team/info`, `/team/list` | `team_endpoints.py:1665`, `/team/list` `:6692` |
| Users | `POST /user/new`, `/user/update`, `/user/delete`; `GET /user/info`, `/user/list` | `internal_user_endpoints.py:527`, `/user/list` `:2424` |
| Models | `POST /model/new`, `/model/update`, `/model/delete`; `PATCH /model/{model_id}/update`; `GET /model/info`, `/v1/model/info` | `model_management_endpoints.py:3213`, `:3441`, `:1746`; info `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:19054` |
| Config | `POST /config/update`, `/config/field/update`; `GET /config/list` | hidden from OpenAPI; DB required; `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:21457`, `:21942` |
| Cache | `/cache/ping`, `/cache/delete`, `/cache/flushall`, `GET /cache/redis/info`, `/cache/settings` | prefix `litellm/proxy/caching_routes.py:20-23`; settings `management_endpoints/cache_settings_endpoints.py:453` |

# 10 — Quality Gates and profiles

## 1. Quality Gate: role and default

[all] A Quality Gate (QG) answers "is the project ready to release?" via metric conditions (metric + operator + error value); one failure fails it. Conditions target new code or overall code; projects without an association get the instance default QG (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/quality-standards-administration/managing-quality-gates/introduction-to-quality-gates.md).

Built-in **Sonar way** is the default, read-only QG with four new code conditions: no new issues (or reliability/security/maintainability ratings worse than A), 100% hotspots reviewed, coverage ≥80%, duplication ≤3% (source: same URL). Two QGs are built in; creating/editing custom ones requires *Administer Quality Gates* (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/quality-standards-administration/managing-quality-gates/managing-custom-quality-gates.md).

*Fudge factor*: duplication conditions ignored up to 20 new lines, coverage up to 20 lines to cover; global default, per-project override. Tests affect only Maintainability/Reliability metrics (Standard: Code Smells/Bugs); duplication and security in test code are not measured.

**Commercial**: conditions on *prioritized rules* exist only in SonarQube Server; **AI Code Assurance** (QG qualified for AI code) is absent from Community Build — Developer/Enterprise/Data Center only (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/feature-comparison-table.md).

## 2. Create, copy, associate

UI: **Quality Gates → Create** copies Sonar way conditions; **Copy** duplicates; **Rename**/**Delete** manage lifecycle. Edit via **Unlock editing → Add Condition** (new/overall code, metric, failure value). Association: QG administrator or project manager (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/quality-standards-administration/managing-quality-gates/managing-custom-quality-gates.md). Standard ↔ MQR switching may require revisiting conditions; Sonar way updates automatically.

Web API controller: `api/qualitygates` (source: `server/sonar-webserver-webapi/src/main/java/org/sonar/server/qualitygate/ws/QualityGatesWs.java:45`). Confirmed actions: `create`, `copy`, `rename`, `destroy`, `list`, `search`, `show`, `select`, `deselect`, `set_as_default`, `add_condition`, `update_condition`, `delete_condition`, `project_status`. Search pagination uses `pageSize` (source: `server/sonar-webserver-webapi/src/main/java/org/sonar/server/qualitygate/ws/QualityGatesWsParameters.java:44`).

```bash
export SONAR_URL=http://localhost:9000
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SONAR_TOKEN" "$SONAR_URL/api/qualitygates/list"
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SONAR_TOKEN" \
  "$SONAR_URL/api/qualitygates/project_status?projectKey=my:project"
```

`api/qualitygates/project_status` is the canonical pipeline status read; alternatively the scanner polls with `sonar.qualitygate.wait=true` (default `false`, timeout 300 s).

## 3. New code period: definitions and real parameters

NCD: Previous version, Number of days (default 30, max 90), Specific analysis or Reference branch; global baseline default is Previous version, the project definition prevails (source: https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-community-build/user-guide/about-new-code.md).

Web API controller `api/new_code_periods` (source: `server/sonar-webserver-webapi/src/main/java/org/sonar/server/newcodeperiod/ws/NewCodePeriodsWs.java:39`), actions `set`, `unset`, `show`, `list`; `set` takes `project`, `branch`, `type`, `value` (source: `server/sonar-webserver-webapi/src/main/java/org/sonar/server/newcodeperiod/ws/SetAction.java:57-60`). ## 2. Backends and defaults

Accepted types: `local`, `redis`, `redis-semantic`, `valkey-semantic`, `s3`, `qdrant-semantic`, `azure-blob`, `gcs` (`litellm/types/caching.py:10-18`). `Cache(...)` built directly is `type=local` (`litellm/caching/caching.py:131`); the proxy turns `cache: True` with no `cache_params` into `redis` (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:7175`) and fills host/port/password from `REDIS_HOST`, `REDIS_PORT`, `REDIS_PASSWORD` (`:7183-7190`).

Docs still list `type: disk`/`disk_cache_dir`, but the backend was removed: it only logs "Ignoring disk_cache_dir, the disk cache backend was removed" (`:340-341`), and an unknown type raises `ValueError: Unsupported cache type` (`:338-341`).

TTL: `cache_params.ttl`, `default_in_memory_ttl`, `default_redis_ttl` (`:6809-6813`). Plain `cache: True` caches `/chat/completions`, `/completions`, `/embeddings`, `/audio/transcriptions`, `/rerank`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`; the list is `cache_params.supported_call_types` (`litellm/caching/caching.py:142`, `https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/caching.md`).

## 3. Exact versus semantic

Exact-match caches (`redis`, `s3`, `gcs`, `local`) hash the call's model-API params (`litellm/caching/caching.py:410-461`); any conversation change misses — right for agentic traffic.

Semantic caches (`redis-semantic`, `valkey-semantic`, `qdrant-semantic`) embed the prompt and serve the closest stored response above `similarity_threshold`; hits carry `x-litellm-semantic-similarity`. Prompt content is excluded from the key (`:377-381`), so isolation rides on the tenant scope appended to it (`:396-408`, `:446-447`) — virtual key, team, organization; every end user behind one key shares a bucket unless `semantic_cache_scope: end_user` (`litellm/types/caching.py:21-23`). The docs target it at single-shot prompts: multi-turn or agentic traffic replays stale responses (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/caching_semantic.md`).

## 4. Multi-worker correctness

A per-process cache means four workers keep four caches and the hit rate "drops roughly by the worker count" (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/caching.md`); every enforced counter splits the same way (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/redis_requirements.md`):

| Without Redis | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| rpm/tpm/max parallel (key, team, user) | Effective limit multiplied by worker count |
| Budgets | Spend reserved per worker; hard budgets overshoot |
| Cooldowns, usage/latency routing | One worker's traffic only |
| Key/team revocation | Revoked key works until local expiry |
| Scheduled jobs | No pod lock; every worker runs it |

Redis is a correctness requirement once `--num_workers > 1` or replicas > 1.

The exact-match cache stays keyed on the request alone, so two keys sending identical requests share a response unless you set `cache.namespace` or `metadata.redis_namespace`; only the semantic cache is tenant-scoped (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/security_owasp_llm_top10.md`).

## 5. Controls and invalidation

Per request, `cache` accepts `ttl`, `s-maxage` (only entries younger than N seconds), `no-cache`, `no-store`, `namespace` (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/caching_controls.md`).

- **Spend writes.** Batch (`proxy_batch_write_at: 60`); above ~1K RPS use the Redis transaction buffer (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/db_sizing.md`).
- **Admission control.** `general_settings.max_in_flight_requests_per_worker` turns overload into a fast 503 with `retry-after`; `max_queued_requests_per_worker` and `admission_queue_timeout_seconds` set the queue. Off until the cap is set; per worker process (4 × 64 admits 256). A stream holds its slot to the last chunk; health and `/metrics` bypass the gate (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/server_tuning.md`).
- **Sizing.** `db.m7g.xlarge` to 1K RPS, `2xlarge` to 5K, `4xlarge` to 10K, `8xlarge` to 20K (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/db_sizing.md`); Redis from `https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/redis_sizing.md`; published throughput is a starting point, not a promise (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/benchmarks.md`).

# 11 — Admin UI

Scope: what `/ui` can do on a free gateway, how admins sign in, where UI writes land, and where a YAML-owned key or missing database makes a UI edit impossible. Dashboard `[OSS]`; SSO and organization pages `[Enterprise]`.

## 1. What `/ui` is

A pre-built Next.js static export mounted with Starlette (`app.mount("/ui", StaticFiles(directory=ui_path, html=True), name="ui")`) — read-only HTML plus client-side JS. Every button calls a proxy REST endpoint on the same origin, so the UI can never do what the API cannot.

- Packaged export: `litellm/proxy/_experimental/out` (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:2742`). Boot resolution: packaged path, then `/var/lib/litellm/ui` when `LITELLM_NON_ROOT=true`; `LITELLM_UI_PATH` wins (`:2847-2855`). `_next` is mounted twice, then `/ui` (`:2970-2982`).
- `DISABLE_ADMIN_UI=True` serves "Admin UI Disabled" instead of the dashboard (`litellm/proxy/common_utils/admin_ui_utils.py:8`).
- Extensionless routes (`/ui/login`) need each exported `*.html` moved to `<route>/index.html`; the proxy does that at boot only when the UI directory is writable, so read-only deployments must pre-build it or those routes break (`:2920-2931`).
- Needs a master key and `DATABASE_URL`; without the DB the key, team, and user pages fail (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/ui.md`).

## 2. Sign-in paths

`POST /login` is the hidden form handler (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:20106`).
## 3. What an OSS admin can do

Route tree under `litellm/ui/litellm-dashboard/src/app/(dashboard)/`:

| Page route | Capability | Endpoint it drives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models-and-endpoints` | Add/edit/delete DB models, no restart (`https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/ui.md`) | `POST /model/new`, `/model/update`, `/model/delete` |
| `api-keys` | Issue/edit/block/rotate virtual keys | `/key/generate`, `/key/update`, `/key/block` |
| `teams`, `users` | Teams, members, internal users | `/team/*`, `/user/*` |
| `usage`, `logs` | Spend and request logs | `/spend/logs` (`litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_management_endpoints.py:3479`), `/spend/logs/ui` (`:2578`) |
| `playground` | Chat against configured models | `/v1/chat/completions` |
| `caching` | Cache backend and semantic scope | `GET/POST /cache/settings` (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/cache_settings_endpoints.py:453`) |
| `guardrails`, `guardrails-monitor` | Guardrail config and run history | `/guardrails/*` |
| `mcp-servers` | Register MCP servers, tool access | `/mcp/server` (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/mcp_management_endpoints.py:1388`) |
| `router-settings`, `budgets`, `policies`, `workflows` | Router tuning, budgets, policies | `/router/settings` (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/router_settings_endpoints.py:87`), `/budget/*`, `/policy/list` (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/policy_endpoints/endpoints.py:473`) |

The `[Enterprise]` `organizations` page answers 403 without a license: the organization router is built with `_enterprise_license_required` (`litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/organization_endpoints.py:104-119`), message "Organizations are only available for LiteLLM Enterprise users".
